annotations.text:
Three revamps, three different bets.

Each one attacks a problem the current build actually has:

· 8 tabs is a lot of navigation for a game where you mostly ping-pong between clues, map and notes.
· The mobile notebook permanently owns 40% of the screen.
· Clues are a flat grid, so the relationships between leads — the actual detective work — live only in players' heads.

Same case content in all three (The Prized Meeple) so you can compare like for like.

A · DOSSIER
Keep the world, cut the chrome.

Eight tabs collapse to three folder tabs — Brief / Investigate / Reckoning. Directory, Informants, Map and Papers stop being destinations and become lookups you pull up over your work, because that's how you actually use them.

The notebook is a drawer with a handle, not a permanent column.

WHY: you said you like the current look. This keeps that identity and fixes the structure underneath it.

TRADEOFF: the most conservative of the three. Textures still cost legibility on a phone, and skeuomorphism can tip into kitsch if the materials get any heavier.

B · EVIDENCE BOARD
Navigation becomes space, not tabs.

One infinite corkboard. Clues are pinned cards you drag; red string links leads you think connect; the map and the newspaper are objects on the board, not tabs. Notes get pinned where they're relevant instead of filed in a column.

On a phone it becomes a single vertical thread with the string still linking beats.

WHY: it makes deduction the interface. Nothing else here would feel like a genuinely new product.

TRADEOFF: much the biggest build, and the riskiest. Five people dragging one board needs conflict rules you don't currently have, and the phone version is a real compromise rather than the same idea shrunk.

C · GASLIGHT
Strip the texture, let the writing carry it.

Cool blue-black instead of warm brown, one gaslight-amber accent, and no parchment at all. One lead at a time at a proper reading size — this is a game you read, and right now the textures fight the prose.

Tabs move to a slim rail; on mobile the notebook is a pull-up sheet, so the case gets the whole screen.

WHY: fixes the mobile problems structurally rather than tuning around them, and the type does the atmosphere instead of the background.

TRADEOFF: the furthest from what you have now, and it trades away most of the Victorian charm. If the typography isn't strong it just reads as another dark app.
